items.title: 68251_Teddy McRae oral history interview
items.q: Like Foots Thomas always told me, he say, 'Why don't you study with me just six months so I can just say that you studied with me?'

ctx.x: All right. What qualities did you look for in -- Or, did a musician have to have, because there wasn't much personnel changes. Garvan Bushell came into the band and so forth. But what qualities that you look for, say, between the first alto and the third alto?

Well, most of -- One time we had a thing called "a million dollar reed section." And I can tell you the qualities of he men that played in that band. We had a thing called a million dollar reed section. We would have like Foots Thomas, Hilton Jefferson, Chauncy Haughton -- maybe Waymon Carver. Maybe Waymon would come in on baritone. Or, if Duke was in town we would use canely on baritone. whip I would sit in on maybe fourth tenor, (inaudible) would

items.title: 68251_Teddy McRae oral history interview
items.q: the saxophone players, there's Walter Thomas, and Jeff and myself -- we started cleaning that section out.

ctx.x: I say, "Look, there's a little few things that I don't know, and you got some good things here, if we just put them together -- we work on them."

So we -- the saxophone players, there's Walter Thomas, and Jeff and myself -- we started cleaning that section out. Got that section sounding big and strong. And they sound like a saxophone section. Everybody playing, you know.
The trumpet players started taking a little break after shows and getting together and cleaning up their book.
